q: What is artificial intelligence, in the simplest terms used in this chapter?
options: Smart computers that think and reason like humans
Specialized satellite sensors used for high-resolution imaging
A statistical method for measuring soil moisture levels
A pricing model that determines data access costs
explain: Artificial intelligence is described as smart computers that think like humans, helping them recognize patterns, learn from examples, provide suggestions, and make decisions.

q: What distinguishes machine learning from being told every explicit rule?
options: A system requiring no data at all to function
Learning from many labeled examples with human supervision
A system that can only process images, not text
Simply another name for agentic AI systems
explain: Machine learning is AI that learns from many examples (data) with human supervision instead of being told every rule.

q: What is the key difference between deep learning and machine learning described in this chapter?
options: An approach that cannot use labeled data at all
A field entirely unrelated to machine learning
Using layers to find patterns in raw data without given features
A method that only works with numerical data
explain: Deep learning is a type of machine learning that uses layers to process and recognize patterns from unstructured data without human supervision; labels are provided in both, but in deep learning features are not provided to computers.

q: What can generative AI models create?
options: Only numerical predictions from structured datasets
Only satellite imagery captured by orbiting sensors
Only spreadsheets containing organized tabular data
Multimedia content, including text, images, sound, and video
explain: Generative AI refers to deep learning models that can create multimedia content, including text, images, sounds, and videos.

q: What are foundation models, and what are some examples?
options: Large AI models trained on vast data, able to perform many tasks
Small models trained narrowly for one specific task
Physical hardware components mounted on a satellite
A specific type of vegetation index formula
explain: Foundation models are very large generative AI models trained on vast amounts of data, able to perform a variety of tasks. ChatGPT, Gemini, or Claude are examples of foundation models.

q: What does agentic AI use as its basis to act as a helper for a specific area?
options: Raw, unprocessed satellite imagery with no further processing
Foundation models that provide broad, general-purpose knowledge
Radar sensors mounted on ground-based farm equipment
Vegetation index values calculated in prior seasons
explain: Agentic AI systems use foundation models to target a specific area as helpers, learning new information, creating plans, and even assisting with tasks.

q: What can AI help agronomists do regarding plant stress?
options: Detects stress only after it causes crop failure
Physically removes stressed plants from the field
Replaces the need for physical sensors entirely
Identifies the type, level, and severity of stress, and forecasts its progression
explain: AI can help agronomists identify the type, level, and severity of stress, and forecast how it will act in the future.

Processes only plain text input, nothing else
A satellite platform equipped with multiple sensors
A vegetation index combining several spectral bands
explain: Multimodal models are AI models that can work with multiple data types simultaneously, such as text, images, audio, and video.

q: What happens after a model is trained on annotated data?
options: Tested and validated to confirm it performs accurately
Immediately deployed with no further review
The training data is permanently deleted
Development ends permanently at that point
explain: After training, the model is tested and validated to ensure the model is performing accurately, before being deployed to be used in the field.

q: Why is AI model development described as a cyclical process?
options: Trained models are never actually deployed
Developers keep learning new things throughout the process, forming a cycle
It repeats identical steps with no new learning
It only applies specifically to satellite-derived data
explain: Throughout this process AI developers may learn new things about the data, methods used in training, or new technology, so the process forms a development cycle for continual improvements.
